title: Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis
answer: Evidence extraction, weighing the consensus, questions over your own sources, broad scans and translating between fields.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are the structured grids that turn individual research reports into comparable rows and columns for a literature review or evidence synthesis.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus is the practice of assessing how much agreement actually exists across a body of research, rather than assuming that a large number of papers equals a settled finding.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources is the habit of auditing the evidence base of a review you are writing or have already published, rather than trusting the citations you have accumulated.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents and landscape scans cover the use of autonomous or semi-autonomous software to plan, run and report on broad literature searches.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines in evidence synthesis means making concepts, measures, and findings from one field legible to another without flattening their meaning.

sections.body: Literature review and evidence synthesis is the work of turning a pile of papers into a defensible account of what is known. AI systems now help by extracting study details into structured tables, grouping claims by topic, and flagging where findings agree or conflict. They can scan preprints and journal articles at a scale no single reader manages, then draft summaries that a human checks against the source. The site's extraction work has produced 13,608 claims from research works, which shows both the promise and the volume problem. These tools do not replace reading, because a model can miss context, methods, or caveats that change the meaning of a result. The useful pattern is guided by a human, with AI doing triage and assembly while a researcher owns the judgment.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has made real progress on extraction, because models can pull population, intervention, outcome, and effect size from many paper formats with reasonable accuracy. It has also made progress on clustering claims and visualizing consensus, though consensus itself is a social and statistical judgment, not a fact a model can simply read off. What remains unsolved is deep appraisal: judging risk of bias, handling contradictory results, and knowing when a literature is too thin to support a conclusion. Models still hallucinate citations, misread tables, and overstate certainty when a paper is exploratory. Broad scans can surface relevant work across fields, but they can also bury the key paper under plausible noise. The honest limit is that synthesis is an argument about evidence, and no automated pipeline can make that argument on its own.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section form a workflow from raw papers to cross field insight. Evidence Extraction Tables is where a reader goes for the mechanics of turning a study into rows and columns that can be compared. Weighing the Scientific Consensus helps with the next step, judging what a body of work actually supports when studies point in different directions. Questioning Your Own Sources is the check on that confidence, asking whether the papers you found are the right ones and whether your search missed contrary evidence. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans covers the broad sweep, the automated passes that map a field before you narrow down. Translating Between Disciplines is for the harder move, carrying a method or finding from one field into another without losing its meaning, and together they describe a loop, not a line, because each page sends the reader back to the evidence with a sharper question.
